_readme: Disambiguation notes for gazetteer terms. Annotates risky entries in the companion .txt files; does NOT replace them. Schema: term (lowercase, matches automaton term_lower) | kinds (colliding gazetteer kinds) | risk (low/medium/high/critical) | region_hint | requires_coevidence (OR-groups of lowercase co-occurring tokens; sentence window preferred) | negative_coevidence (OR-groups whose presence votes AGAINST the gazetteer sense) | confidence_penalty (0-1) | default_kind (winner on conflict, null = flag ambiguous) | action (keep/gate/demote/remove) | notes. POLICY: nothing is removed for being ambiguous — every risky term gets a contextual identification rule instead. Feeds the future mapping DB population (terms table 1:1). v1 seed — extend as precision reviews demand.

_policies.applies_to: any gazetteer term of 3 or fewer characters (li, ma, hu, he, yu, du, ye, su, lu, wu, xu, na, min, ...)
_policies.rule: Never annotate a bare short token. Accept only with at least one coevidence: honorific or title adjacent (mr/mrs/ms/dr/prof/st/sir/lady), biographical verb in the same sentence (born/died/married/appointed/graduated/succeeded), a Capitalized+Capitalized pair whose partner is itself gazetteer-known, an attribution verb nearby (said/says/told/according to/stated), or an initial pattern (X. Yyyy). Apply confidence_penalty 0.45 when only weak (single-pair) evidence exists.
_policies.rationale: Two-letter tokens collide with pronouns (he), verbs (du/do), abbreviations (min/minute, na/sodium, ma/mother/MA-state, su/sue, yu/you). Context, not the token, carries the signal.

_policies.applies_to: multi-word place names composed of ordinary descriptive words (beautiful valley, pleasant point, saltwater creek, ...)
_policies.rule: Require Title Case on every word AND at least one of: a geographic preposition within 5 tokens (in/at/near/nearby/around/throughout/across/just outside), a regional coevidence term in the same sentence (country, state, or known city), or a gazetteer-neighbor place in the same sentence. Lowercase or isolated occurrences stay unannotated.
_policies.rationale: Descriptive phrases are real places but read as ordinary prose. Capitalization plus geographic framing distinguishes 'we camped at Beautiful Valley' from 'a beautiful valley stretched ahead'.

michael OR river OR basketball OR bulls

Substring hazard: fires inside 'Papua New Guinea' / 'Equatorial Guinea' / 'Guinea-Bissau' alongside the full name. Annotator rule: on overlapping spans prefer the LONGEST match, drop the subsumed one.
Substring hazard inside 'South Sudan'. Longest-match rule applies; bare Sudan defaults to Sudan (not South).

requires_coevidence: texas OR cowboys OR mavericks OR dfw

requires_coevidence: florida OR dade OR south beach OR hurricanes

requires_coevidence: colorado OR broncos OR nuggets OR mile high OR john

requires_coevidence: massachusetts OR celtics OR red sox OR harvard OR mit

NOT in gazetteers (deliberately excluded: UK city vs universal verb). Documents the exclusion policy: high-frequency common words stay out of flat lists even when they are real places; mapping phase resolves via co-evidence instead.

requires_coevidence: augusta OR portland OR bangor OR pine tree OR new england OR lobster OR governor
notes.notes: US state vs adjective 'main' in 'the maine attraction' style wordplay and the historic province of Maine (France). Capitalized bare Maine in US-geographic context is usually the state; require state coevidence, else flag.

requires_coevidence: santiago OR andes OR south america OR spanish OR atacama OR valparaiso
notes.notes: Country vs chili pepper (common misspelling 'chile'). Food coevidence (recipe, pepper, spicy, relleno, con carne) means NOT the country — treat as negative evidence.

requires_coevidence: beijing OR dynasty OR ming OR great wall OR mandarin OR communist OR shanghai
notes.notes: Country vs fine porcelain ('china cabinet', 'china cups'). Tableware coevidence (cabinet, cups, plates, dishes, set) is negative evidence for the country sense.

requires_coevidence: peru OR south america OR andes OR ohio OR allen county
notes.notes: Capital of Peru (and Lima, Ohio) vs lima bean. Food coevidence (beans, soup, succotash, butter) is negative evidence.

requires_coevidence: portugal OR douro OR gaia OR portuguese
notes.notes: Portuguese city vs port wine ('porto', 'port') and generic harbour noun. Wine coevidence (tawny, vintage, bottle, wine) is negative evidence for the city sense.

requires_coevidence: alaska OR cook inlet OR denali OR alaskan
notes.notes: Alaskan city vs ordinary noun (harbour anchorage, mooring). Lowercase or nautical coevidence (harbour, mooring, anchor, vessel) means the noun — the city is virtually always capitalized with Alaska context.

requires_coevidence: italy OR italian OR emilia OR towers OR university
notes.notes: Italian city vs bologna sausage. Food coevidence (sandwich, meat, slice, oscar mayer) is negative evidence.

requires_coevidence: italy OR arno OR leaning OR tower OR tuscany
notes.notes: Italian city vs PISA education test (usually ALL-CAPS). All-caps PISA near students/scores/education is the test, never the city — treat casing as evidence.

requires_coevidence: arizona OR maricopa OR desert OR suns OR cardinals
notes.notes: City vs mythical bird and countless business names. City sense dominates in geographic text; myth sense comes with rising/ashes/rebirth coevidence.

requires_coevidence: new zealand OR southland OR stirling point OR invercargill OR oyster
notes.notes: NZ town vs poker/deception verb ('bluffing', 'called his bluff'). Verb forms and card-game coevidence are negative evidence.

requires_coevidence: new zealand OR canterbury OR timaru OR south canterbury
notes.notes: NZ township vs ordinary noun (caves, spelunking, stalactite). Lowercase or plural/caving coevidence means the noun.

al OR vice president OR climate OR tipper OR election

baptist OR catholic OR methodist OR parish OR street OR avenue OR road
notes.notes: Surname vs org-suffix vs ordinary noun — triple collision and case variants collapse in matching. Org sense needs a multi-word capitalized name before it; person needs person coevidence; generic 'the church' phrases are negative evidence for both.

requires_coevidence: city OR county OR parish OR national OR security OR tribal

notes.notes: Rare surname vs event noun. Event sense needs a named treaty ('Treaty of X', signed/ratified nearby); surname needs person coevidence.

requires_coevidence: natural gas OR british gas OR company OR corp OR station
notes.notes: Org suffix vs everyday noun/verb. Bare 'gas' is never an organization alone — require a capitalized company body (British Gas, Gazprom-styled names) or drop.

requires_coevidence: company OR corp OR petroleum OR crude OR shell OR bp
notes.notes: Same rule as gas: bare 'oil' is a commodity noun, never an org. Require company-form coevidence.

requires_coevidence: university OR national OR research OR los alamos OR bell OR laboratory
notes.notes: Clipping of laboratory; only safe after a capitalized institution name. Bare 'lab' is generic.

requires_coevidence: national OR central OR world bank OR of america OR chase OR hsbc OR reserve
